1.word_for_word: tri-catvāriṃśake — in the forty-third chapter; gajendram hatvā — after killing the king of elephants; rāma-kṛṣṇayoḥ raṅga-praveśa-saubhāgyam — the splendor of Rāma and Kṛṣṇa entering the arena; cāṇūreṇa bhāṣaṇam — Cāṇūra's speech; pūrva-edyuḥ eva kṛtam śaucam — their innocence had already been established the previous day; dhanur-bhaṅga-ādinā nija-aiśvarye sūcite api — though they had indicated their power by breaking the bow and other deeds; pitarau na muñcati — Kaṃsa still would not release their parents; āvām punaḥ jighāṃsati — and still sought to kill them; asya mātulasya vadhe na doṣaḥ — hence there is no fault in killing their maternal uncle; malla-dundubhīnām nirghoṣam — the roar of the wrestlers' drums
1.translation: The forty-third chapter describes the killing of the royal elephant, the splendor of Rāma and Kṛṣṇa entering the arena, and Cāṇūra's speech. Their innocence had already been established the previous day: even after they displayed their divine power by breaking the bow and other acts, Kaṃsa still refused to release their parents and continued trying to kill them. Therefore no blame would attach to them for killing their maternal uncle. The opening also refers to the booming sound of the wrestlers and their drums.

2.word_for_word: ambaṣṭhaḥ — elephant-driver; hasti-pakaḥ — mahout; tena coditam — urged on by him
2.translation: ‘Ambaṣṭha’ here means the elephant-driver or mahout; the elephant was urged forward by him.

3.word_for_word: parikaram — battle dress; yuddha-ucita-paridhānam — clothing suited to combat; kṛtvā — arranging it; samuhya — gathering up; nibadhya — tying securely
3.translation: Kṛṣṇa arranged his clothing into a battle-ready dress, gathering it up and tying it securely.

5.word_for_word: antakaḥ — death; kālaḥ — Time, the occasion of death; yamaḥ — the ruler of death; taiḥ upamā yasya — compared with these
5.translation: The elephant is compared with Antaka, death itself, with Time as the occasion of death, and with Yama, its ruling lord.

6.word_for_word: vigalitaḥ — slipped away; vicyutaḥ — escaped; muṣṭinā nihatya — striking with his fist; alīyata — disappeared; adṛśyaḥ babhūva — became unseen
6.translation: ‘Vigalita’ means that Kṛṣṇa slipped or escaped from the elephant's grasp. After striking, he disappeared from its view.

7.word_for_word: acakṣāṇaḥ — not seeing; ghrāṇam avaghrāṇam — smell, sniffing; tena dṛṣṭiḥ yasya — using smell as its means of perception; locana-agocaram api paśavaḥ ghrāṇena jānanti — animals know by scent what is outside the range of sight; parāmṛśat — seized; puṣkareṇa — with the tip of the trunk; sa kṛṣṇaḥ — that Kṛṣṇa; prasahya — forcibly; balena — with strength
7.translation: Unable to see Kṛṣṇa, the elephant used its sense of smell as its guide, for animals are known to detect by scent what lies beyond their vision. It seized him with the tip of its trunk, but Kṛṣṇa resisted and acted by force.

8.word_for_word: pañca-viṃśatiḥ dhanuṣām — twenty-five bow-lengths; tāvantam deśam vicakarṣa — dragged it that distance; nāgam sarpa-vat vartamānam gajam — the elephant moving like a serpent; suparṇa-vat svayam — Kṛṣṇa like Garuḍa; upamā — comparison
8.translation: Kṛṣṇa dragged the elephant a distance of twenty-five bow-lengths. The comparison is that the elephant, though itself a nāga, moved helplessly like a serpent, while Kṛṣṇa dragged it like Garuḍa dragging a snake.

9.word_for_word: puccha-grāhiṇam śrī-kṛṣṇam grahītum — trying to catch Kṛṣṇa who held its tail; dakṣiṇataḥ parivartate — when the elephant turned right; savyataḥ bhrāmayati — Kṛṣṇa swung left; savyataḥ parivartate — when it turned left; dakṣiṇataḥ bhrāmayan — he moved right; go-vatsena bhrāmyamāṇena bālakaḥ iva — like a boy playing with a calf
9.translation: As the elephant tried to turn and catch Kṛṣṇa, who held its tail, Kṛṣṇa always moved to the opposite side—left when it turned right and right when it turned left—circling with it like an ordinary boy playing by turning a calf around.

10.word_for_word: vāraṇam gajam — the elephant; prādravan — running vigorously around it; pātayām āsa — caused it to fall; yathā patati tathā tam vañcayan — deceiving it so that it fell
10.translation: Kṛṣṇa ran swiftly around the elephant, eluding it in such a way that it was made to fall.

11.word_for_word: sa dhāvan — while it ran; ahanat — struck; ahan — he hit it
11.translation: The sense is simply that while the elephant charged, Kṛṣṇa struck it.

15.word_for_word: raṅgam samāviśat — entered the arena; vīra-śriyā babhau — shone with heroic beauty; aṃse nyastam viṣāṇam — elephant tusk placed on his shoulder; asṛjaḥ raktasya madasya ca bindubhiḥ aṅkitaḥ — marked with drops of blood and rut-fluid; virūḍhāḥ sveda-kaṇikāḥ — beads of sweat arisen; vadana-amburuham — lotus face
15.translation: When Kṛṣṇa entered the arena he shone with heroic splendor. An elephant tusk rested upon his shoulder; drops of blood and the elephant's rut-fluid marked his body, and newly risen beads of sweat adorned his lotus-like face.

16.word_for_word: na kevalam sa ekaḥ samāviśat — he did not enter alone; vṛtau gopaiḥ — the brothers were surrounded by the cowherds
16.translation: He did not enter alone; the two brothers entered surrounded by the cowherds.

17.word_for_word: śṛṅgāra-ādi-sarva-rasa-kadamba-mūrtiḥ — embodiment of the whole cluster of rasas beginning with erotic love; tat-tad-abhiprāya-anusāreṇa babhau — appeared according to each observer's disposition; na sākalyena sarveṣām — not identically to all; mallādīnām ajñānām draṣṭṝṇām — to the wrestlers and other unknowing spectators; aśani-ādi-rūpeṇa daśadhā viditaḥ — perceived in ten distinct ways, beginning as a thunderbolt; rasāḥ — emotional flavors; raudraḥ adbhutaḥ śṛṅgāraḥ hāsyam vīraḥ dayā bhayānakaḥ bībhatsaḥ śāntaḥ sa-prema-bhaktikaḥ — fury, wonder, love, humor, heroism, compassion, fear, disgust, peace and loving devotion; aviduṣām virāṭ vikalaḥ — to the ignorant, an incomplete or merely material cosmic person; bībhatsa-rasaḥ — disgust
17.translation: Bhagavān is the embodiment of the entire cluster of rasas, yet in the arena he appeared to each observer according to that person's own disposition rather than showing every rasa equally to all. The wrestlers and other unknowing spectators perceived him in ten distinct ways, beginning with the force of a thunderbolt. Śrīdhara lists the corresponding rasas as fury, wonder, erotic love, humor, heroism, compassion, fear, disgust, tranquility and loving devotion. The ignorant who regarded him merely as an extraordinary material person experienced the rasa of disgust or incongruity; their mistaken sense of his disproportion is later expressed in the objection that the boys' bodies and the wrestlers' bodies are utterly unmatched.

18.word_for_word: udvivije — became frightened; bhītaḥ babhūva — was afraid

19.word_for_word: yathā naṭau — like two actors; nirbhayatvam darśitam — this expresses their complete fearlessness
19.translation: The comparison ‘like two actors’ indicates the brothers' complete fearlessness and ease.

20.word_for_word: praharṣa-vegena utkalitāni — opened wide by a surge of joy; īkṣaṇāni ānanāni ca — eyes and faces; tayoḥ ānanam papuḥ — they drank the two brothers' faces; param na tṛptāḥ — yet were not satisfied; nirākāṅkṣāḥ na babhūvuḥ — their longing did not cease
20.translation: A surge of joy made the spectators' eyes and faces open wide. They seemed to drink the faces of Rāma and Kṛṣṇa, yet they never became satisfied; their longing to look did not cease.

21.word_for_word: pibantaḥ iva — as if drinking; śliṣyantaḥ — as if embracing; pariṣvaṅgam kurvantaḥ iva lakṣitāḥ — appearing as though physically clasping them
21.translation: The expressions ‘as if drinking’ and ‘as if embracing’ mean that through their intense gaze the spectators appeared almost to drink and physically embrace the brothers.

22.word_for_word: yathā-dṛṣṭam dhanuḥ-bhaṅga-ādi — what they had seen, such as the breaking of the bow; yathā-śrutam govardhana-uddharaṇa-ādi — what they had heard, such as lifting Govardhana; tad-anurūpam — in conformity with those reports; pratyakṣam tayoḥ rūpam gaja-danta-ādi-yuktam — their visible appearance bearing elephant tusks and the like; guṇāḥ śaurya-ādayaḥ — qualities such as valor; mādhuryam hasita-ālāpa-ādi — sweetness in smiles and speech; prāgalbhyam dhārṣṭyam — bold confidence; taiḥ smāritāḥ iva — as though reminded by these
22.translation: What the people now saw corresponded perfectly with what they had already seen, such as the breaking of the bow, and what they had heard, such as the lifting of Govardhana. The brothers' visible form carrying elephant tusks, their qualities such as valor, their sweetness in smiles and speech, and their fearless boldness all brought those earlier accounts vividly back to mind.

23.word_for_word: vismitānām vākyāni — statements of the astonished spectators; aṣṭabhiḥ — in eight verses; etau iti-ādibhiḥ — beginning with ‘these two’
23.translation: The next eight verses give the words spoken by the astonished spectators, beginning with ‘These two…’

24.word_for_word: kila iti — the particle kila; sarvatra anvayaḥ — it is to be understood throughout the series
24.translation: The particle ‘kila,’ conveying report or common knowledge, is to be carried through the statements that follow.

25.word_for_word: guhyakaḥ — the Guhyaka; śaṅkhacūḍaḥ — Śaṅkhacūḍa; anye ca — and the others; aghāsura-ādayaḥ — beginning with Aghāsura
25.translation: The Guhyaka mentioned is Śaṅkhacūḍa; the ‘others’ include Aghāsura and the other demons.

28.word_for_word: āśramam — slightly weary; īṣat-śrama-yuktam mukham — a face showing a trace of fatigue; aśramam mukham iti vā — alternatively, a face entirely without fatigue; yad vā aśramam yathā bhavati tathā taranti sma — alternatively, they crossed over without fatigue
28.translation: The word may mean that their faces showed only the slightest fatigue, or, under another reading, that they were entirely without fatigue. A further construction takes the phrase adverbially: they crossed through the ordeal without weariness.

29.word_for_word: anena parirakṣitaḥ yadoḥ vaṃśaḥ — the Yadu dynasty protected by him; su-bahu-viśrutaḥ san — becoming widely renowned; śrī-ādi lapsyate — will attain prosperity and the rest
29.translation: The speakers say that the Yadu dynasty, protected by Kṛṣṇa, will become exceedingly renowned and attain prosperity and other blessings.

30.word_for_word: dhenuka-baka-vatsāsureṣu — in the stories of Dhenuka, Baka and Vatsāsura; viparyaya-uktiḥ — reversal or variation in the wording; jana-vādeṣu — in popular reports; ari-cayāt — because of variation in the enumeration of enemies
30.translation: The variation in how Dhenuka, Baka and Vatsāsura are mentioned reflects differences in popular retellings and in the order in which the defeated enemies were enumerated.

31.word_for_word: janeṣu evam bruvāṇeṣu — while the people were speaking in this way; tad asahamānaḥ cāṇūraḥ — Cāṇūra, unable to tolerate it; abravīt — spoke
31.translation: While the people were speaking in this way, Cāṇūra, unable to tolerate their praise, addressed Kṛṣṇa and Rāma.

35.word_for_word: he kṛṣṇa priyam karavāma — O Kṛṣṇa, let us do what pleases the king; rājñi prīte — when the king is pleased; bhūtāni ca prasīdeyuḥ — his subjects or beings too will be pleased
35.translation: Cāṇūra's sense is: ‘O Kṛṣṇa, let us act so as to please the king. When the king is pleased, his subjects also prosper and are satisfied.’

38.word_for_word: yathā-ucitam niyuddham — wrestling matched appropriately; bāhu-yuddham — hand-to-hand combat; malla-sabhā-sadaḥ — officials or members of the wrestling assembly; adharmaḥ mā spṛśet — let no injustice touch them; he malla iti vā — alternatively, direct address ‘O wrestler’
38.translation: The wrestling should be properly matched, a fair contest of bodily strength, so that the officials of the wrestling assembly are not implicated in injustice. The wording may also be read as a direct address, ‘O wrestler.’

39.word_for_word: sahasra-dvipānām sattvam balam — the strength of a thousand elephants; bibharti — he bears; iti tathā — hence the description
39.translation: The phrase means that he possessed the strength of a thousand elephants.

40.word_for_word: balibhiḥ mādṛśaiḥ saha — with strong men such as me; anayaḥ adharmaḥ — no impropriety or injustice; vikrama parākramam kuru — display your prowess; muṣṭikaḥ vikramatāt — and let Muṣṭika display his strength
40.translation: Cāṇūra argues that there is no injustice in matching the brothers with powerful men such as himself: ‘Show your prowess against me, and let Muṣṭika likewise display his strength.’
